name: Hip Adduction Machine
description: The hip adduction machine is a seated machine exercise that works the inner thigh adductors by pressing the knees inward against pad resistance. The adductor magnus, adductor longus, adductor brevis, and gracilis are the primary movers. The machine isolates the adductors by removing the balance requirements of standing adduction exercises, and provides consistent resistance through the entire range of motion.

execution.starting_position: Sit in the hip adduction machine with back against the pad. Place legs on the outer sides of the pads with knees and ankles against the pad surfaces. Set pads to a wide starting position.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust seat height and pad width for a comfortable starting stretch. Use a weight that allows full range of motion.
steps: Step 1: Sit in the machine with back flat, legs on outer sides of pads. Begin with pads in the wide starting position.
Step 2: Press both legs inward — adducting the hips — by squeezing the inner thighs.
Step 3: Press until the pads are as close together as the machine allows.
Step 4: Hold the peak contraction briefly.
Step 5: Return slowly to the wide starting position under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you press the legs together. Inhale as you open.
common_mistakes: Using momentum — slow, controlled movement throughout
Not controlling the eccentric — the opening phase should be slow
Rounding the lower back against the pad
safety_considerations: Avoid if the exercise causes groin strain — reduce range or weight
Start conservatively — the adductors can be strained if loaded aggressively without warm-up
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Open to a comfortable stretch at the start. Close fully at the end.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the inner thighs — not the glutes
Control the opening — resist the pads on the way out
Keep the back flat — don't lean forward
